questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 42-year-old lady presented with sudden onset severe headache, aphasia, and diplopia. Imaging shows an empty delta sign of superior sagittal sinus thrombosis. Choose the correct statement about the dural fold containing the affected sinus.

options.text: It separates the cerebellum from the occipital lobes of the cerebrum.
It separates the two cerebellar hemispheres.

questions.explanation: The superior sagittal sinus lies in the falx cerebri. Falx cerebri separates the two cerebral hemispheres; its upper fixed margin contains the superior sagittal sinus, its lower free margin the inferior sagittal sinus, and its attachment to tentorium cerebelli contains the straight sinus. Tentorium separates cerebellum from occipital lobes; falx cerebelli separates cerebellar hemispheres and contains the occipital sinus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with chronic otitis media and mastoiditis develops thrombosis of the sinus marked below. Which of the following sinuses does it drain from?
questions.explanation: The marked sinus is the sigmoid sinus, which continues from the transverse sinus. It follows an S-shaped groove near the mastoid, receives mastoid and condylar emissary veins, the venous plexus of the hypoglossal canal, inferior cerebellar veins and other tributaries, and joins the inferior petrosal sinus to form the internal jugular vein. Sigmoid/lateral sinus thrombosis can complicate ear or mastoid infection.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A diabetic lady with a history of chronic sinusitis presents with seizures and altered mental status. On examination, she is febrile and you note a left-sided lateral rectus palsy. On fundoscopy, papilledema is present bilaterally. Which of the following is not a tributary of the sinus involved here?
questions.explanation: The presentation suggests cavernous sinus thrombosis. The deep middle cerebral vein is not a tributary; it joins other deep cerebral veins to form the basal vein. Tributaries of the cavernous sinus include superior/inferior ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus, superficial middle cerebral vein and inferior cerebral vein. The source also lists drainage routes and contents including the cavernous ICA, sympathetic plexus, abducens nerve and lateral-wall cranial nerves.
